title: Retrofit call facade: OpenAI tool schema → legacy function adapter
creator: Sofia Patel
description: We need a runtime-level facade that lets OpenAI-style tool calls (name + JSON-schema) interoperate with Redwood's older legacy function surface used by internal integrations and some long-lived customers. Problem: many clients still construct 'function' calls with arg shapes and names that differ from the newer tool manifest conventions; we must avoid breaking them while supporting streaming, structured outputs, and deterministic fallbacks. Goal: implement a translation/adaptor layer that can be enabled per-customer and per-route to normalize names, coerce parameters, preserve streaming semantics (chunked events + partial tool outputs), and emit telemetry for mismatch frequency. This ticket covers design, a first-pass implementation, tests, and a canary release to Dedicated customers.
technical_design: Facade sits in the request router before the runtime's tool dispatcher. Key parts: (1) Name alias registry: static + telemetry-driven aliases; resolves incoming tool name to canonical tool id using exact, case-insensitive, and fuzzy Levenshtein match with threshold and an alias score. (2) Schema translator: mapping rules (rename, optional-to-required heuristics, type coercion with safe guards) driven by a per-tool mapping table and lightweight transforms expressed as JSONPath mappings. (3) Streaming passthrough: when a tool call is marked streamable, the facade maintains chunk framing and converts tool output events into the legacy function streaming frames expected by older clients, preserving event ordering and backpressure signals. (4) Safety and fallback: if a strict schema check fails, the facade can fall back to a permissive marshalling mode (controlled by route flag) and attach a compatibility warning header to the response. (5) Observability: attach request-level tags for alias match type, coercions applied, and fallbacks used. Implementation notes: small stateful cache for alias resolutions with TTL 6h; the mapping tables stored in Config Service and editable via Console; translation functions implemented in Rust for runtime performance with a thin Go API layer for routing integration.
acceptance_criteria: Exact-name tool calls route to canonical tool id with zero-coercion and pass existing unit tests
Minor-name mismatches (case, underscores) auto-resolve with alias score >= 0.9 and are recorded in telemetry
Schema coercion rules convert string->int and number->string where safe; unsafe conversions rejected unless permissive mode enabled
Streaming tool outputs are delivered to legacy clients with preserved chunk order and same latency SLO as non-translated calls (max 20ms added p50)
Admin can view and edit mapping table in Console and changes take effect within 2 minutes
Canary rollout to 3 Dedicated customers with feature flag succeeds and no customer-reported regressions after 48h
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests; 2) Integration tests against a legacy-function emulator; 3) Internal canary behind feature flag for infra team; 4) Gradual Dedicated customer canary (3 tenants) with telemetry gates; 5) Enable for self-serve customers by default after 2 weeks of stable telemetry. Rollback: flip off feature flag or switch to strict reject mode if mismatch rate > 2% and error budget consumed.
telemetry: Emit metrics: alias_match_type{exact,ci,fuzzy}, coercion_applied_count, fallback_mode_count, streaming_frame_rewrite_latency_ms, compatibility_warnings_emitted. Dashboards: per-route heatmap of alias traffic, top mismatched names, per-customer rollback rate. Add logging of representative examples to a capped sample store (1000/day) for ops review.
risks: Incorrect coercions can produce silent data corruption for downstream tools; fuzzy-name resolution may accidentally alias distinct tools if threshold too low. Mitigations: telemetry + sampling of transformed payloads, strict-by-default with opt-in permissive mode, and an admin 'dry-run' where transformations are logged but not applied.
qa_plan: Create a legacy-function emulator that verifies stream framing, ordering, and backpressure. Add fuzz tests that generate near-miss names and parameter shapes. Run e2e test matrix: {exact,ci,fuzzy} x {strict,permissive} x {streaming,non-streaming}. Verify Console mappings UI shows edits and that changes propagate to runtime.
